rule: Every receipt audit export must map to a tenant-scoped backend storage record before production learning persistence begins.
phase_one_guardrail: No rental payment, deposit, escrow, payout, booking commission, payment-custody signal, tenant-private memory, or unscoped audit record can reach production storage in phase one.
storage_principles: Map every export-ready receipt to a backend audit table before implementation.
Keep tenant id, record id, receipt event, export scope, storage route, row policy, retention policy, rollback state, and blocked route together.
Separate tenant-private proof payloads from aggregate-safe audit metadata.
Require row-level policy before any audit record can be read across roles.
Store blocked payment-custody routes as guardrails, not monetization signals.
Make retention and rollback rules visible before storage begins.
Keep the storage plan static and testable until a real database exists.

role_storage_plans.rollback_state: restore prior rank if proof is disputed
restore prior visibility if proof expires
restore prior market queue if response drops

acceptance: Marketplace shows Backend Audit Storage after Receipt Audit Export.
Buyer, supplier, and founder views each show table, tenant scope, write route, read route, row policy, retention policy, rollback state, and blocked route.
Copy output explains storage event, source export, tenant scope, write route, read route, row policy, retention, rollback, and blocked payment route.
Build Phase shows the v177 Backend Audit Storage Plan contract after the Receipt Audit Export contract.
Docs include storage states, storage routes, blocked payment routes, and required storage fields.
Static check fails if the storage UI, contract, JSON model, cache-bust token, or render functions are missing.
No production learning persistence can begin without a tenant-scoped storage plan or explicit hold.
